input.goal: Fix the review-pipeline bugs: run_pipeline only processes part of the submitted task list; multi-task runs finalize immediately instead of pausing for human review; resume_after_review restarts or loses state instead of continuing the reviewed thread; thread state must be isolated by thread_id. Keep public function names unchanged and keep test_pipeline.py unchanged.

grill.summary: Grilling session completed on the real frontier; user agreed to all eight decisions. Q1: review gate is uniform - run_pipeline pauses for review whenever require_review=True and there is at least one task; require_review=False finalizes immediately. Q2: __interrupt__ carries a self-describing dict payload {reason: human_review, thread_id, tasks}. Q3: all tasks are processed and results stored in THREADS[thread_id] before pausing; the interrupt stops finalization/summary, not execution (pause before summary, AC-2). Q4: resume_after_review raises KeyError on an unknown thread_id instead of silently returning an empty approval. Q5: after resume the thread state is retained and status flips to approved; repeated resumes idempotently return the same results. Q6: calling run_pipeline again on an existing thread_id starts fresh and overwrites that thread's state. Q7: an empty task list finalizes immediately ('finalized 0 task(s)') even with require_review=True. Q8: module-private helpers may be added; public names run_pipeline, resume_after_review and THREADS, their signatures/defaults, and test_pipeline.py stay untouched. Facts verified by the host (not asked of the user): THREADS is a module-global dict keyed by thread_id; test_pipeline.py is the only consumer; baseline pytest shows 4 failures matching AC-1..AC-4; local Markdown tracker under .scratch/grill-test/; test command python -m pytest test_pipeline.py -q. User confirmed shared understanding and empty frontier in the host session.
